summary.judgment: The three qa-final1 defects are fixed: demo labels are legible in dark mode, the raw SVG now has readable mobile typography, and component figures no longer create nested figure markup. The lesson remains mathematically and pedagogically strong. Final sign-off is withheld because the live demo produces a React hydration mismatch from server/client floating-point SVG coordinates; in mobile dev preview the resulting Next issue overlay overlaps the first preset row.

qa-final1.json and the current lesson-cycle evidence relevant to its three fixes

render_and_interaction_evidence.chapter_preview: npm run preview -- digital-signal-processing dft-bins-symmetry-and-scaling completed and generated light/dark chapter and figure sheets.
render_and_interaction_evidence.desktop_light_dark: All four authored visuals were visually inspected in both themes; formulas, labels, plots, ledgers, semantic colors, and captions remain unclipped and coherent.
render_and_interaction_evidence.mobile_light_dark: The live lesson was inspected at a 360x900 CSS-pixel viewport in light and dark themes. documentElement.scrollWidth equaled 360, so no page-level horizontal overflow was present.
render_and_interaction_evidence.dark_demo_labels: All six required preset labels computed to rgb(234, 234, 230) in dark mode and rgb(25, 25, 24) in light mode. Their controls retain 44 CSS-pixel height and readable active/inactive states.
render_and_interaction_evidence.raw_svg_mobile_typography: At 360 CSS px the raw SVG renders 312 px wide, selects .mobile-layout, hides .desktop-layout, and scales its 23-24 viewBox-unit labels by 0.4875, yielding 11.21-11.70 CSS px. The axis, k row, X[4]=8, and signed-hertz ledger are legible in both themes.
render_and_interaction_evidence.semantic_markup: The live lesson contains 5 figure elements and 5 figcaptions (four authored visuals plus the demo), with document.querySelectorAll('figure figure').length === 0. RealDftConventionLedger and PaddingDurationResolution now return neutral div roots.
render_and_interaction_evidence.demo_behavior: The lab starts alive on Padded pair with N=64, Q=16, L=1024 and a two-phase FAIL; Coarse tone advanced by keyboard to Q=4 reaches f-hat=172.00 Hz and e_bin=0.0625; Padded pair remains unresolved at a 1 Hz grid; Long pair holds L=1024 and reports two-phase PASS with acquired N=256.
render_and_interaction_evidence.regression: The browser console reports 'A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties.' The diff is confined to raw floating-point y2/cy attributes in PaddingVsDataLab (for example 189.67238647809046 client versus 189.67238647809043 server). Next's mobile dev issue badge visibly overlaps the first preset row.

checks: The N=4 audits give [0,2,0,2] and [2,0,2,0], and the stated inverse samples are correct.
The N=8 and N=6 half-open signed-frequency maps, including the even-N Nyquist singleton, are correct.
The real-input rule X[(N-k) mod N]=X*[k], endpoint doubling exceptions, phased cosine coefficients, and composite-signal coefficients are correct.
The scale family alpha beta N=1, the raw/unitary/forward-scaled values, and both Parseval forms are internally consistent.
The linear/circular convolution examples and N >= L_x+L_h-1 padding boundary are correct.
The off-bin cosine coefficients and conjugate pairs were independently checked and do refute the stated false claim.
The padding lab reproduces 0.1875 bins at Q=1, 0.0625 at Q=4, short-record failure, and long-record success.
The final exercise correctly derives X[k]=E[k]+W_8^k O[k] and X[k+4]=E[k]-W_8^k O[k].

exercise_audit.parallel_pair: The worked x=[1,0,-1,0] row audit is immediately followed by the parallel x=[1,0,1,0] exercise.
exercise_audit.earlier_concept_required: Closing Exercise 3 requires the prerequisite finite-record DTFT model and recalls it with a Ref.
exercise_audit.forward_evidence: Only closing Exercise 6 derives even/odd reuse and links the result to FFT Factorization and Machine Layout.

rubric.criterion: Opening precisely states the problem in declarative sentences
rubric.evidence: 'The DFT samples one period of a finite record's spectrum and therefore inherits both periodic indexing and implementation conventions.' It is verbatim from course.yaml and contains no question or tease.

rubric.criterion: Concrete instance precedes formalism
rubric.evidence: Before the first Definition, the lesson computes the inherited N=8 cosine and its concrete coefficient list '[0,0,4,0,0,0,4,0]'.

rubric.criterion: Everything serves the single stated goal
rubric.evidence: The route declares the transform, labels bins, handles real symmetry, audits scale, distinguishes circular convolution, and separates padding from observation; every move serves computing and interpreting a finite DFT contract.

rubric.criterion: Chapter is substantial
rubric.evidence: The chapter derives inversion, conjugacy, Parseval, and circular convolution; treats endpoint cases and three normalization families; and closes with six mixed solved exercises.

rubric.criterion: Environments are honest and hypotheses explicit
rubric.evidence: The roots-of-unity theorem begins 'For a positive integer N and integers k and ell'; both theorems include real proofs, and definitions include boundary and near-miss cases.

rubric.criterion: Most exercises require mathematical production and include a parallel problem
rubric.evidence: Learners compute, diagnose boundaries, refute, derive, choose representations, and factor; '[1,0,1,0]' is parallel to the worked '[1,0,-1,0]' audit.

rubric.criterion: Earlier concepts are required and confusable types are mixed
rubric.evidence: Exercise 3 requires the earlier finite-record DTFT, while Exercise 5 makes the learner choose reversible storage versus amplitude reporting without naming the method in advance.

rubric.criterion: Every solution shows a complete path and no trick questions
rubric.evidence: All ten Exercises have Solutions with equations, convention decisions, checks, and interpretations; none depends on an unstated convention.

rubric.criterion: At most one mechanical closing exercise
rubric.evidence: Only closing Exercise 1 is a direct DFT/inverse audit; Exercises 2-6 require boundary reasoning, refutation, derivation, representation choice, or factorization.

rubric.criterion: At least two difficulty-floor archetypes
rubric.evidence: The set contains a boundary probe, a plausible false claim to refute, and a derivation omitted from the body.

rubric.criterion: Exactly one forward closing exercise with Ref
rubric.evidence: Only Exercise 6 reaches forward, and its Solution says the linked FFT lesson 'formalizes this reuse recursively as the radix-two FFT'.

rubric.criterion: Callouts pass the deletion test
rubric.evidence: The retrieval Aside supplies otherwise absent answers; the strongest boundary KeyFact preserves the operational N=2 '[-1,1]' versus padded N=3 '[1,1,-2]' contrast.

rubric.criterion: No citation appears for its own sake
rubric.evidence: Body Ref links carry continuity; secondary surveys remain in the chapter-precise References block.

rubric.criterion: No narration of the obvious or flavor idiom
rubric.evidence: Lead-ins such as 'compute the full linear output first, then reduce its indices modulo' identify a mathematical decision rather than narrating visible notation.

rubric.criterion: Each visual carries an idea and remains usable
rubric.evidence: The four captions state claims, all visuals carry distinct ideas, mobile compositions do not clip, and the repaired raw SVG's load-bearing labels render at 11.21-11.70 CSS px at 360 px.

rubric.criterion: Demo reveals dynamic behavior, starts alive, and supports the stated task
rubric.evidence: The lab starts on an informative unresolved pair, keyboard/touch controls complete every stated target, and dark labels now use rgb(234,234,230). However, live hydration reports server/client SVG-coordinate mismatches and the resulting mobile dev issue overlay overlaps the first preset row; deterministic rendering is required before sign-off.

rubric.criterion: Cadence and section subdivision
rubric.evidence: No run exceeds three substantive prose paragraphs without a heading, environment, callout, table, or visual; long sections have descriptive ### breaks.

rubric.criterion: Fold-stripped skeleton reconstructs the argument
rubric.evidence: The skeleton runs 'Eight correlations become one declared transform' -> 'A bin acquires hertz...' -> 'Real records halve storage...' -> 'Scaling is an interface contract' -> 'DFT multiplication wraps...' -> 'More plotted bins do not add observation'.

rubric.criterion: Typed emphasis and em-dash discipline
rubric.evidence: Bold marks payoff terms such as 'acquisition aperture' and 'circular convolution'; italics introduces the one-sided spectrum; code marks fftshift; em-dash use is sparse.

rubric.criterion: Dry engineering register
rubric.evidence: 'High array indices therefore do not mean high positive physical frequencies' typifies the declarative register; there are no rhetorical questions, teases, personas, or chatty asides.

rubric.criterion: References are real, relevant, and chapter-precise
rubric.evidence: Entries route to Oppenheim-Schafer §§8.4-8.7/10.1-10.2, Lyons §§3.1-3.14, MIT Sessions 17-18, and Schaedler Lessons 15/21-25/28; the MIT scale translation is explicit.

rubric.criterion: Lessons 1-2 are the gentlest polished entry
rubric.evidence: Single-lesson review of lesson 8; whole-course entry polish was not scored.

rubric.criterion: Whole-course spiral coverage
rubric.evidence: Single-lesson review; whole-course spiral coverage was not scored.

rubric.criterion: Whole-course scope, outcomes, and technical titles
rubric.evidence: Single-lesson review; only the target lesson's goal and spine alignment were assessed.

rubric.criterion: Paragraph after opening places the move in the course argument
rubric.evidence: It says Sampling ended with eight correlations, DTFT established their continuous periodic curve, and this lesson turns them into a complete finite coordinate system.

rubric.criterion: Section seams chain the running question
rubric.evidence: Sampled seams inherit unresolved facts: 'The coefficient index becomes a frequency coordinate only after...', 'The negative-frequency half is redundant..., but...', and 'The continuous DTFT theorem maps..., but...'.

rubric.criterion: Last content section hands off consistently with the spine
rubric.evidence: The close inventories the complete coefficient contract and hands repeated roots of unity, operation count, order, and scaling to the FFT lesson.

rubric.criterion: Headings carry claims where possible
rubric.evidence: 'Real records halve storage, not the transform', 'Scaling is an interface contract', and 'More plotted bins do not add observation' are claim headings.

rubric.criterion: Two sampled body sections pass the cover test
rubric.evidence: Without seam and final sentences, the scale body still derives alpha beta N=1 and Parseval; the padding body still controls N versus L and evaluates phase stability.

rubric.criterion: Immediate predecessor closing joins the opening
rubric.evidence: The predecessor ends with '[0,0,4,0,0,0,4,0]' and promises indexing, hertz, normalization, symmetry, and circular interpretation; the target immediately inherits that list.

rubric.criterion: No mid-prose secondary-survey attribution
rubric.evidence: No body sentence says that a textbook 'describes' the material; named surveys remain in References.

rubric.criterion: Places and events are anchored
rubric.evidence: No geographic places or historical events occur in this mathematics lesson.

rubric.criterion: Named-term load is controlled
rubric.evidence: New terms arrive in separate beats: DFT pair, signed bin map, one-sided amplitude report, normalization, circular convolution, and zero padding.

rubric.criterion: Earlier material is recalled with Ref and reminder
rubric.evidence: The opening Ref clauses remind what Sampling and DTFT established, and the convolution section recalls zero-extended linear convolution with a Ref before use.

rubric.criterion: Numeric prose carries its frame
rubric.evidence: Numbers carry N, f_s, units, denominators, phase sets, or consequences in the same sentence, as in 'f_s=1024 samples/s...N=64...spacing 16 Hz'.

rubric.criterion: Keeper numbers are identifiable and privileged
rubric.evidence: N=8 coefficient audits live in figures, while the boundary KeyFact preserves the memorable '[-1,1]' versus '[1,1,-2]' result.

rubric.criterion: No data-row narration of human events
rubric.evidence: No human-event evidence occurs.

rubric.criterion: Body details pass the deletion test
rubric.evidence: The 3/16 and 1/16 errors drive the lab target; 0 and 90 degrees test stability; N=64/256 isolates duration; N=2/3 drives the boundary inference.

rubric.criterion: Sourced rasters pass visible-not-legible
rubric.evidence: The lesson uses no sourced raster images.

rubric.criterion: Real misconceptions are explicitly refuted
rubric.evidence: The lesson replaces bins-as-tone-detectors with finite-record DTFT sampling and replaces padding-as-resolution with controlled transform-length versus acquired-length evidence.

rubric.criterion: Importance is marked by device shift, not intensifiers
rubric.evidence: Definitions, Theorems, Examples, Tasks, Aside, KeyFacts, and Exercises keep distinct roles; no intensifier substitutes for structure.
